title: Sessions on Claude Sonnet 5 from September 2026 are priced at an increase the provider cancelled
foundBy: session agent, while auditing the cost estimates in a rendered trace against the provider's published price list on 2026-09-19, at the host's request

evidence.verified: `go test ./internal/normalizer/ -run TestEmbeddedTableSonnet5HasNoSeptemberReprice -count=1`: PASS. A million input and a million output tokens cost $12 for a session started in August 2026 and for one started in September 2026. A real Sonnet 5 subagent session from September, normalized with the rebuilt binary, estimated $0.49, which matches a hand sum at the published rates.

resolution: The `claude-sonnet-5` entry is one undated rate set at $2 input and $10 output. The dated-rates mechanism stays, and its own test still covers it with a synthetic table.
details:
The `claude-sonnet-5` entry in `pricing.json` carries two dated rate periods. The first runs through 2026-08-31 at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. The second starts 2026-09-01 at $3 and $15, with the cache rates scaled to match.

The table was audited on 2026-08-03, when the provider had announced that increase. The provider now says the introductory rate is the standard one, and that the increase will not happen.

Every Sonnet 5 session started on or after 2026-09-01 is therefore estimated at 1.5 times its real cost.

To reproduce, render a Sonnet 5 session started in September 2026 and recompute its cost from its token totals at $2, $10, $0.20, $2.50 and $4.

The fix is one undated rate set at the introductory numbers. The `_doc` line that describes the reprice needs to say what happened instead.

notes.text: An announced reprice is a claim about the future. The `_doc` line on dated rates now says to recheck one after its date has passed.
